subject: chem
title: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
syllabus: Purification — crystallisation, sublimation, distillation, differential extraction and chromatography — principles and their applications. Qualitative analysis — detection of nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and halogens. Quantitative analysis (basic principles only) — estimation of carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, halogens, sulphur, phosphorus. Calculations of empirical formulae and molecular formulae; numerical problems in organic quantitative analysis.

topics.est: Estimation of C, H, halogens, S, P; formulae

body: Sublimation: solid → vapour → solid. Crystallisation: solubility difference. Distillation: boiling-point difference
Simple distillation: large b.p. gap (chloroform + aniline). Fractional: close b.p. (crude oil). Reduced pressure: decomposes at its b.p. (glycerol from spent-lye).
Steam distillation: steam-volatile and water-IMMISCIBLE (aniline, essential oils, o-nitrophenol); it distils when p_{water} + p_{organic} = 1 atm, below 373 K.
Differential extraction: shake with an immiscible solvent in which the compound is more soluble. Purity check: sharp m.p./b.p.

check.why: It decomposes at its normal b.p.

body: R_{f} = distance moved by the compound / distance moved by the solvent front (0 < R_{f} < 1)
Adsorption chromatography (column, TLC): silica gel or alumina. Polar compounds stick more → lower R_{f}; in a column the least adsorbed comes out first.
Partition chromatography (paper): water trapped in the paper is the stationary phase. Colourless spots: UV light, iodine vapour, or a spraying reagent (ninhydrin for amino acids).
Fuse with Na: N → NaCN, S → Na_{2}S, X → NaX, P → Na_{3}PO_{4}. N needs C too, so hydrazine gives no test.
N: FeSO_{4}, boil, then FeCl_{3}/H_{2}SO_{4} → Prussian blue Fe_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}]_{3}. S: sodium nitroprusside → violet; or lead acetate → black PbS.

N + S together: NaSCN → blood red with Fe^{3+}. Halogens: boil with HNO_{3} (destroy CN^{−}, S^{2−}), then AgNO_{3}: AgCl white (NH_{3}-soluble), AgBr pale yellow, AgI yellow. P: ammonium molybdate → yellow.
Dumas: % N = (28/22400) × V_{STP}(mL)/w × 100, with V_{STP} from (P − aqueous tension)V/T. Kjeldahl: % N = 1.4 × (milli-equivalents of acid used)/w
Dumas heats the compound with CuO (in CO_{2}); N_{2} is collected over KOH. Kjeldahl digests with conc. H_{2}SO_{4} (CuSO_{4} catalyst, K_{2}SO_{4}) → (NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4} → NH_{3} into standard acid.
Kjeldahl fails for nitro, azo and ring nitrogen (pyridine). 1 mol H_{2}SO_{4} neutralises 2 mol NH_{3}.

body: Combustion: H_{2}O absorbed in anhydrous CaCl_{2}, CO_{2} in KOH. Carius: heat with fuming HNO_{3} (+AgNO_{3} for halogens). O is found by difference.
Empirical formula: % ÷ atomic mass → divide by smallest → whole numbers. Molecular formula = n × empirical, n = M/empirical mass.

traps: Subtract aqueous tension in Dumas before using PV = nRT.
H₂SO₄ is dibasic: 1 mol neutralises 2 mol NH₃.
Kjeldahl does not work for pyridine, nitro or azo compounds.
Steam distillation needs a water-IMMISCIBLE liquid.
Paper chromatography is partition, not adsorption.
Reducing pressure LOWERS the boiling point.
N and S together give blood red, not Prussian blue.

pyq.q: In Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, CuSO_{4} acts as :
sol: The compound is digested with conc. H_{2}SO_{4}; CuSO_{4} (with K_{2}SO_{4} to raise the boiling point) only speeds up the conversion of N to (NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4}.
So CuSO_{4} is a catalyst.

pyq.q: Lassaigne's test is used for detection of :
sol: Fusing with Na turns covalent N, S, halogens and P into NaCN, Na_{2}S, NaX and Na_{3}PO_{4}.
All four are then tested in the sodium fusion extract.

pyq.q: Following Kjeldahl's method, 1 g of organic compound released ammonia, that neutralised 10 mL of 2M H_{2}SO_{4}. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ______ %.
sol: mol H_{2}SO_{4} = 0.020; it neutralises 2 × 0.020 = 0.040 mol NH_{3}.

pyq.q: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.5 gram of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound (Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg) is ______%
sol: Dry N_{2} pressure = 715 − 15 = 700 mm Hg.

pyq.q: During estimation of nitrogen by Dumas' method of compound X (0.42 g) [X = piperazine, a six-membered ring –CH_{2}CH_{2}–NH–CH_{2}CH_{2}–NH–] ______ mL of N_{2} gas will be liberated at STP. (nearest integer) (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} : C : 12, H : 1, N : 14)
sol: Piperazine C_{4}H_{10}N_{2}, M = 86; each molecule gives one N_{2}.

pyq.q: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen 0.4 g of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is (Given : Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mmHg )

In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen 1 g of an organic compound gave 150 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 900 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is ______ % (nearest integer) (Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg )
Which of the following nitrogen containing compound does not give Lassaigne's test ?
sol: The N test needs CN^{−} in the fusion extract: Na + C + N → NaCN.
Hydrazine (NH_{2}NH_{2}) has no carbon → no NaCN → no Prussian blue.

pyq.q: In Dumas' method 292 mg of an organic compound released 50 mL of nitrogen gas (N_{2}) at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of 'N' in the organic compound is ______ % (Nearest integer) (Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mmHg )

Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : Kjeldahl method is applicable to estimate nitrogen in pyridine. Statement (II) : The nitrogen present in pyridine can easily be converted into ammonium sulphate in Kjeldahl method. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
sol: Ring nitrogen (pyridine), nitro and azo nitrogen are not converted to (NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4} by digestion.
So Kjeldahl fails for pyridine — both statements are false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : Nitrogen, sulphur, halogen and phosphorus present in an organic compound are detected by Lassaigne's Test. Statement (II) : The elements present in the compound are converted from covalent form into ionic form by fusing the compound with Magnesium in Lassaigne's test. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: true — all four are detected in the fusion extract.
II: false — the compound is fused with sodium metal, not magnesium.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lassaigne's test, the covalent organic molecules are transformed into ionic compounds. Statement II: The sodium fusion extract of an organic compound having N and S gives prussian blue colour with FeSO_{4} and Na_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}] In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: true — Na converts them to NaCN, Na_{2}S, NaX.
II: false — with N and S together, NaSCN forms and gives a blood-red colour with Fe^{3+}, not Prussian blue.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements I and II. Statement-I : Dumas method is used for estimation of "Nitrogen" in an organic compound. Statement-II : Dumas method involves the formation of ammonium sulphate by heating the organic compound with conc H_{2}SO_{4}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: I: true. II: false — Dumas heats the compound with CuO and collects N_{2} gas; forming (NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4} with conc. H_{2}SO_{4} is Kjeldahl.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Appearance of blood red colour, on treatment of the sodium fusion extract of an organic compound with FeSO_{4} in presence of concentrated H_{2}SO_{4} indicates the presence of element/s
sol: N and S together give NaSCN in the fusion extract.
SCN^{−} + Fe^{3+} → [Fe(SCN)]^{2+}, blood red.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Aniline reacts with con. H_{2}SO_{4} followed by heating at 453 − 473 K gives p − aminobenzene sulphonic acid, which gives blood red colour in the 'Lassaigne's test'. Statement II: In Friedel - Craft's alkylation and acylation reactions, aniline forms salt with the AlCl_{3} catalyst. Due to this, nitrogen of aniline aquires a positive charge and acts as deactivating group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: sulphanilic acid contains both N and S → NaSCN → blood red with Fe^{3+}. True.
II: the Lewis acid AlCl_{3} binds the –NH_{2} lone pair, making –NH_{2}^{+}AlCl_{3}^{−}, a deactivating group. True.
o: Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both statement I and statement II are true

pyq.q: When 1 g of compound (X) is subjected to Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, 15 mL 1 M H_{2}SO_{4} was neutralized by ammonia evolved. The percentage of nitrogen in compound (X) is :
sol: 15 mL of 1 M H_{2}SO_{4} = 0.015 mol → neutralises 0.030 mol NH_{3}.

pyq.q: In Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.50 g of an organic compound gave 70 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K and 715 mm pressure. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is ______ %. (Aqueous tension at 300 K is 15 mm ).

0.5 g of an organic compound on combustion gave 1.46 g of CO_{2} and 0.9 g of H_{2}O. The percentage of carbon in the compound is ______ . (Nearest integer) [Given : Molar mass (in g mol^{−1}) C : 12, H : 1, O : 16 ]
In Carius method, 0.75 g of an organic compound gave 1.2 g of barium sulphate, find percentage of sulphur (molar mass 32 g mol^{−1}). Molar mass of barium sulphate is 233 g mol^{−1}.

Consider the reaction sequence: benzene → (conc. HNO_{3} + conc. H_{2}SO_{4}, 333 K) P → (1. Sn/HCl/Δ; 2. pH neutralised) Q → ((CH_{3}CO)_{2}O) R → (conc. HNO_{3} + conc. H_{2}SO_{4}) S (major product) → (1. HCl/EtOH, Δ; 2. pH neutralised) T. The percentage of nitrogen in product 'T' formed is ____%. (Nearest integer) (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16)
sol: P nitrobenzene → Q aniline → R acetanilide → S p-nitroacetanilide (–NHCOCH_{3} directs para) → T p-nitroaniline after hydrolysis.

pyq.q: A student has been given 0.314 g of an organic compound and asked to estimate Sulphur. During the experiment, the student has obtained 0.4813 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur present in the compound is ______ . (Given Molar mass in g mol^{−1} S : 32, BaSO_{4} : 233)

A student performed analysis of aliphatic organic compound 'X' which on analysis gave C = 61.01%, H = 15.25%, N = 23.74%. This compound, on treatment with HNO_{2}/H_{2}O produced another compound 'Y' which did not contain any nitrogen atom. However, the compound 'Y' upon controlled oxidation produced another compound 'Z' that responded to iodoform test. The structure of 'X' is :
sol: HNO_{2} turns a 1° amine into an alcohol Y; Y oxidises to a methyl ketone (iodoform +) only if Y is propan-2-ol.
So X = (CH_{3})_{2}CHNH_{2} (a secondary-carbon amine; n-propylamine would give propanal).

pyq.q: Consider the reaction sequence: p-nitrotoluene → (i) Sn/HCl; OH^{−} (ii) (CH_{3}CO)_{2}O (iii) Br_{2}/AlBr_{3} (iv) H_{3}O^{+} → Major Product (P). When the product (P) is subjected to Carius analysis using AgNO_{3}, 1.0 g of the product (P) will produce ______ g of the precipitate of AgBr. (Nearest Integer) (Given : molar mass in g mol^{−1} C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, N : 14, Br : 80, Ag : 108 )
sol: p-Toluidine → acetanilide (protects –NH_{2}) → Br enters ortho to –NHCOCH_{3} → hydrolysis: P = 2-bromo-4-methylaniline, C_{7}H_{8}BrN (M = 186).

pyq.q: Given below are four compounds : (a) n-propyl choride (b) iso-propyl chloride (c) sec-butyl chloride (d) neo-pentyl chloride. Percentage of carbon in the one which exhibits optical isomerism is :
sol: Only sec-butyl chloride CH_{3}CH_{2}CHClCH_{3} has a chiral carbon.

pyq.q: In Carius method for estimation of halogens, 180 mg of an organic compound produced 143.5 mg of AgCl. The percentage composition of chlorine in the compound is ______%. (Given: molar mass in g mol^{−1} of Ag : 108, Cl : 35.5 )
sol: 143.5 mg AgCl is 1 mmol → 35.5 mg Cl.

pyq.q: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.15 g of silver bromide (AgBr). The percentage of Bromine in the organic compound is ______ × 10^{−1}% (Nearest integer). (Given : Molar mass of Ag is 108 and Br is 80 g mol^{−1})

In the sulphur estimation, 0.20 g of a pure organic compound gave 0.40 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is ______ × 10^{−1}%. (Molar mass : O = 16, S = 32, Ba = 137 in g mol^{−1})

2.0 g of a bromo hydrocarbon (X) was subjected to Carius analysis, gave 3.36 g of AgBr. The percentage of carbon in the compound (X) is 26.7%. Total number of carbon atoms in the empirical formula for compound (X) is ____. (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, Br : 80, Ag : 108)
sol: Carbon atoms = 5.

pyq.q: The cycloalkene (X) on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of (X) and gives the product (Y) in which C : Br ratio is 3 : 1. The percentage of bromine in the product (Y) is ____ %. (Nearest integer) (Given : molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, O : 16, Br : 80 )
sol: One Br_{2} adds → 2 Br; C : Br = 3 : 1 → 6 C: cyclohexene → Y = 1,2-dibromocyclohexane C_{6}H_{10}Br_{2} (M = 242).

pyq.q: Sodium fusion extract of an organic compound (Y) with CHCl_{3} and chlorine water gives violet color to the CHCl_{3} layer. 0.15 g of (Y) gave 0.12 g of the silver halide precipitate in Carius method. Percentage of halogen in the compound (Y) is ____ . (Nearest integer) (Given : molar mass g mol^{−1} C : 12, H : 1, Cl : 35.5, Br : 80, I : 127 )
sol: Cl_{2} water frees I_{2} from I^{−} → violet in CHCl_{3}: the halogen is iodine.

pyq.q: In sulphur estimation, 2.0 × 10^{−3} mol of an organic compound (X) (molar mass 76 g mol^{−1}) gave 0.4813 g of barium sulphate (molar mass 233 g mol^{−1}). The percentage of sulphur in the compound (X) is ____ × 10^{−1}% (Nearest integer)

One mole of phenol is treated with dilute HNO_{3} at 298 K to give a mixture of products. The mixture is separated by steam distillation. The steam volatile compound (X) is separated. The increase in percentage of oxygen in (X) with respect to phenol is ____ × 10^{−1}% (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16 )
sol: o-Nitrophenol (intramolecular H-bond) is steam volatile; p-nitrophenol is not. X = C_{6}H_{5}NO_{3}, M = 139.

pyq.q: In Carius method 0.2425 g of an organic compound gave 0.5253 g silver chloride. The percentage of chlorine in the organic compound is

Consider the sequence: diazoaminobenzene (Ph–N=N–NH–Ph) → (i) HCl (ii) Aniline (in excess) (iii) Warm 40–45°C (iv) Cool, acetic acid → Yellow Product (X). The percentage of nitrogen in the yellow product (X) formed is ____ %. (Nearest Integer) (Given Molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, N : 14 )
sol: Diazoaminobenzene rearranges in acid (with aniline) to p-aminoazobenzene, the yellow dye: C_{6}H_{5}–N=N–C_{6}H_{4}–NH_{2}.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Purification technique) with List - II (Mixture of organic compounds): (A) Distillation (simple) (B) Fractional distillation (C) Distillation under reduced pressure (D) Steam distillation; (I) Diesel + Petrol (II) Aniline + Water (III) Chloroform + Aniline (IV) Glycerol + Spent-lye
sol: Simple: large b.p. gap (CHCl_{3} 334 K, aniline 457 K). Fractional: close b.p. (diesel/petrol).
Reduced pressure: glycerol decomposes at its b.p. Steam: aniline is steam volatile and immiscible with water.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Separation of) with List - II (Separation Technique): (A) Aniline from aniline-water mixture (B) Glycerol from spent-lye in soap industry (C) Different fractions of crude oil in petroleum industry (D) Chloroform-Aniline mixture; (I) Simple distillation (II) Fractional distillation (III) Distillation at reduced pressure (IV) Steam distillation
sol: Aniline–water: steam distillation. Glycerol: reduced pressure (decomposes at b.p.).
Crude oil: fractional. Chloroform–aniline: simple distillation.

pyq.q: The adsorbent used in adsorption chromatography is/are A. silica gel B. alumina C. quick lime D. magnesia
sol: NCERT: the common adsorbents are silica gel and alumina.

pyq.q: The correct statements among the following, for a "chromatography" purification method is :
sol: On polar silica/alumina, polar compounds are held more strongly → travel less → smaller R_{f}.
Compounds never outrun the solvent front (R_{f} < 1, a fraction); in a column the non-polar ones come down first.
o: Organic compounds run faster than solvent in the thin layer chromatographic plate.
Non-polar compounds are retained at top and polar compounds come down in column chromatography.
R_{f} of a polar compound is smaller than that of a non-polar compound.

pyq.q: Which of the following statements are correct ? A. Glycerol is purified by vacuum distillation because it decomposes at its normal boiling point. B. Aniline can be purified by steam distillation as aniline is miscible in water. C. Ethanol can be separated from ethanol water mixture by azeotropic distillation because it forms azeotrope. D. An organic compound is pure, if mixed M.P. is remained same.
sol: B is false: steam distillation works because aniline is IMMISCIBLE with water.
A, C (ethanol–water azeotrope, 95.6%) and D (no depression of mixed m.p.) are correct.

pyq.q: Methods used for purification of organic compounds are based on :
sol: The method is chosen from the properties of both the compound and its impurities (volatility, solubility, adsorption …).
o: neither on nature of compound nor on the impurity present.
nature of compound and presence of impurity.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : 1, 2, 3-Trihydroxypropane can be separated from water by simple distillation. Statement (II) : An azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: glycerol decomposes near its boiling point — it is purified by distillation under reduced pressure, so I is false.
II: an azeotrope boils at constant composition, so fractional distillation cannot split it. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The technique used for purification of steam volatile water immiscible substance is:
sol: A steam-volatile, water-immiscible liquid distils with steam below 373 K (p_{water} + p_{organic} = 1 atm).

pyq.q: The purification method based on the following physical transformation is : Solid (X) → (heat) Vapour (X) → (cool) Solid (X)
sol: Solid → vapour directly on heating, vapour → solid on cooling: sublimation (camphor, naphthalene).

pyq.q: Chromatographic technique/s based on the principle of differential adsorption is/are A. Column chromatography B. Thin layer chromatography C. Paper chromatography
sol: Column and thin layer chromatography are adsorption chromatography.
Paper chromatography is partition chromatography (water held in the paper is the stationary phase).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): In partition chromatography, stationary phase is thin film of liquid present in the inert support. Statement (II) : In paper chromatography, the material of paper acts as a stationary phase. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: true — a liquid film on a support is the stationary phase.
II: false — water trapped in the paper is the stationary phase, not the cellulose itself.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Phenol on treatment with CHCl_{3}/aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification produces p-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the major product and o-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the minor product. Statement II: The mixture of p-hydroxybenzaldehyde and o-hydroxybenzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: Reimer–Tiemann gives salicylaldehyde (ortho) as the major product — false.
II: the ortho isomer is H-bonded internally, so it is steam volatile; the para isomer is not. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: On a thin layer chromatographic plate, an organic compound moved by 3.5 cm, while the solvent moved by 5 cm. The retardation factor of the organic compound is ______ × 10^{−1}
sol: R_{f} = distance moved by compound / distance moved by solvent = 3.5/5 = 0.7 = 7 × 10^{−1}.

pyq.q: Which among the following purification methods is based on the principle of "Solubility" in two different solvents?
sol: Differential extraction shakes the aqueous mixture with an immiscible organic solvent in which the compound is more soluble.

pyq.q: 'Adsorption' principle is used for which of the following purification method?
sol: Adsorption (column/TLC) chromatography separates by how strongly each component is held on the adsorbent.

pyq.q: Match List I (Technique) with List II (Application): A. Distillation B. Fractional distillation C. Steam distillation D. Distillation under reduced pressure; I. Separation of glycerol from spent-lye II. Aniline – Water mixture III. Separation of crude oil fractions IV. Chloroform-Aniline
sol: Simple → chloroform/aniline; fractional → crude oil; steam → aniline/water; reduced pressure → glycerol.

pyq.q: The fragrance of flowers is due to the presence of some steam volatile organic compounds called essential oils. These are generally insoluble in water at room temperature but are miscible with water vapour in vapour phase. A suitable method for the extraction of these oils from the flowers is
sol: Steam volatile + water insoluble → steam distillation (they distil below their own b.p., so they do not decompose).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point. Statement II: The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: sublimation is for solids that pass directly into vapour (and non-sublimable impurities) — not "low melting" compounds. False.
II: reducing pressure LOWERS the boiling point (the basis of vacuum distillation). False.
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: Match List - I (Purification technique) with List - II (Used to separate): A. Simple distillation B. Fractional distillation C. Steam distillation D. Distillation under reduced pressure; I. Steam volatile compound II. Two liquids with large difference in boiling points III. Liquid decomposing at its boiling point IV. Two liquids with close boiling points
sol: Simple: large b.p. gap. Fractional: close b.p.
Steam: steam-volatile, immiscible. Reduced pressure: decomposes at its b.p.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: A mixture of C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} (sugar) and NaCl can be separated by dissolving sugar in alcohol, due to differential solubility. Statement II: Rose essence from rose petals is seperated by steam distillation due to its high volatility and insolubility in H_{2}O. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: sugar dissolves in (hot) alcohol while NaCl does not → filter off NaCl. True.
II: essential oils are steam volatile and water-immiscible → steam distillation. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Vapours of the liquid with higher boiling point condense before vapours of the liquid with lower boiling points in fractional distillation. Statement II: The vapours rising up in the fractionating column become richer in high boiling component of the mixture. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: the higher-boiling component condenses first on the column packing. True.
II: so the rising vapour gets richer in the LOWER-boiling component. False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

Statement I is false but Statement II is true
